meta.description: Anima 2B LoRA, background profile (default): batch 1 + grad accumulation 2 (same effective batch as performance; the author's own config uses 4 — see the exposure note at the end), latent + text-embed caching on, low_vram so idle components park on CPU. Leaves VRAM headroom for concurrent desktop use; expect roughly 2-3x the wall-clock of the performance preset. Author's recipe (rank 32, AdamW 2e-5, LLM adapter frozen — upstream's default). The ignore_if_contains list mirrors sd-scripts' Block-only targeting (no LoRA on AdaLN modulation/embedders/final projection) in upstream's diffusers module names. Note: the author's sigmoid_scale 1.3 timestep widening is not supported by upstream's Anima implementation; plain sigmoid timestep sampling is the closest available. Effective batch is a deliberate fork deviation: the author's recipe is accumulation 4, this ships 2, because at effective batch 4 the in-app step suggestion falls under its step floor on a small/medium dataset and gets clamped up — silently inflating real per-image exposure 2-3x past target. Rank/alpha/LR/optimizer are untouched author values; set accumulation back to 4 to reproduce the author's config exactly on a large dataset. If you swap the optimizer to an Automagic variant, this batch-1-plus-accumulation pattern will not work as-is — Automagic fuses its step into the backward pass by default, so gradient_accumulation must go back to 1 and the effective batch reached by raising batch size instead. Speed (2026-08-29): latents are served from RAM after the first pass (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only caching re-read every latent every step), loss_sync_every 4, ui_db_poll_seconds 2. Training math unchanged. STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, added 2026-10-12): 20 images ~1500, 30 images ~2250, 50 images ~3750, 100 images ~6000, then +20/image above 100 (200 images ~6000), capped at 6000. Source: the fork's per-arch advisor value exposure target for anima (steps/image incl. the size damping, i.e. what the exposure gauge calls on-target - before the arch's own maxSteps ceiling) at 20/30/50/100 images, floored at 1500, then +20 steps/image above 100, capped at 6000. Values are steps at effective batch 1 - the Step Suggestion panel and exposure gauge use this table while the preset is loaded and divide by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation); below the first row the first row's steps apply.
